title: optimize-nccl-collectives-and-kvcache-overlap-tp
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Performance: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel throughput and tail latency by tuning NCCL stream priorities, async collectives, kernel scheduling, and KV cache prefetch/eviction heuristics.
description:
Motivation: Tensor-parallel workloads were regularly hitting NCCL synchronization stalls at large batch sizes and long contexts. This PR combines collective tuning with kernel scheduling and KV-cache-aware batching to increase overlap between communication and compute, reduce stall periods, and improve end-to-end throughput for production inference workloads.

Changes included: 1) NCCL tuning: introduce configurable stream prioritization and a lightweight per-collective backoff window to stagger costly all-reduces on skewed workloads. Added async launch paths for reduce_scatter/all_gather where supported by the device driver so collectives can be issued without blocking the main compute stream. 2) Kernel scheduling: extend the runtime scheduler to record per-kernel completion estimates and prioritize small reduction kernels on the high priority stream to minimize blocking of CUDA compute. Added a short-running kernel preemption hint to avoid long kernel monopolization during KV-cache maintenance. 3) KV cache integration: add an active prefetch policy for tensor-parallel layouts that overlaps remote KV exchange with local attention compute; adjust eviction thresholds to avoid pathological thrashing when TP shards are memory-constrained. 4) Continuous batching: update the batching controller to be KV-cache-aware so that prefix-heavy workloads trigger smaller, faster batches that maintain KV locality while still benefiting from batching efficiencies. 5) Tests and telemetry: added microbenchmarks for async collectives and end-to-end TP inference traces; surface new metrics (collective_wait_ms, kv_prefetch_hit_rate, tp_stream_priority_mismatch) for observability and alerting.

Compatibility: No model or API changes. Changes are behind runtime feature flags and can be toggled per-deployment.

Benchmarks: On a 4xA100 (80GB) tensor-parallel 16-way split with 2k context, internal qps/stability tests show +11-14% throughput and 8-12% median latency reduction for streaming inference workloads, with 20-30% reduction in measured collective wait time on workloads that previously had high cross-rank imbalance. Microbenchmarks for async collectives show a 25% reduction in synchronous stall time on average.

Checklist: - [x] NCCL tuning parameters exposed and documented - [x] Scheduler unit tests added - [x] KV cache prefetch unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks and perf dashboards updated - [x] Feature gated and rollout plan documented

Follow-ups: ENG-3620 to extend stream-priority auto-tuning across heterogeneous clusters; ENG-3622 to expose KV prefetch telemetry to Redwood Console for route-level tuning.
